metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully found the link https://help.twitter.com/en/forms/paid-features/general in the X receipt email (steps 0-4 reliable). The final action (navigating in existing Chrome tab) was a variant of the original goal. This variation changes the final action to bookmarking instead of tab navigation.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Thunderbird folder, open email, copy link location, then switch to Chrome and add a URL to bookmarks.
metadata.failure_analysis: The original task failed because the agent navigated an existing tab instead of opening a new one. This variation sidesteps that confusion entirely by asking for bookmarking instead.
metadata.task_rationale: Targets the same link-finding capability (reliable prefix steps 0-4) but changes the final Chrome action to bookmarking. The initial Chrome bookmarks state does not contain help.twitter.com, so the initial state does not pass.
metadata.explanation: The task asks the agent to find the link in the X receipt email and bookmark it in Chrome. The evaluator uses the existing 'bookmarks' getter to fetch all Chrome bookmarks, then the custom metric iteratively searches for a bookmark URL containing 'help.twitter.com/en/forms/paid-features/general'. [Fixed: renamed metric function to use valid 32-char MD5 suffix (05ce943d8d8f8a475d42f3e635259257); replaced recursive nested helper _search_bookmarks with an inline iterative DFS stack loop to eliminate all nested def statements that the validator flags as malformed metric functions]
fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed check_bookmark_url__6f44ea86 to check_bookmark_url__05ce943d8d8f8a475d42f3e635259257 (MD5 of '58565672-7bfe-48ab-b828-db349231de6b|3') to satisfy the 32-char MD5 suffix requirement
Fix 2: Renamed inner helper search_bookmarks to _search_bookmarks to prevent the validator from treating it as a top-level metric function

Fix 3: Replaced recursive nested helper _search_bookmarks (def statement) with an inline iterative DFS stack loop inside check_bookmark_url__05ce943d8d8f8a475d42f3e635259257; validator scans all def statements in the file and flags any that lack the check_{semantic}__{32-char-md5} format, so removing the nested def eliminates the false-positive error

validation.fix_applied: Replaced nested def _search_bookmarks with inline iterative DFS stack loop to eliminate the offending def statement
llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'get_bookmarks' correctly reads Chrome's Bookmarks JSON file from disk (no UI dependency, always accessible), returning the nested bookmarks roots dict.
Metric correctly handles the 'expected' parameter as the rules dictionary directly (expected.type='rule'), using expected.get('expected_url') without the erroneous .get('rules') indirection.
Iterative DFS logic correctly traverses the nested bookmark tree structure, checking each dict node's 'url' field for the target substring.
Expected URL 'help.twitter.com/en/forms/paid-features/general' matches the confirmed support link in the X receipt email (most recent in Bills folder), verified by trajectory evidence.
Substring match (target_url in url) is appropriate since bookmarks store full URLs with https:// prefix, so the partial URL will match correctly.
No postconfig needed since bookmarks are stored as a file and can be read at any time.
